method: Masks are parsed in the browser with exact BigInt arithmetic. Hexadecimal input accepts an optional 0x prefix plus spaces or underscores, ignores leading zeros, and rejects a value wider than 64 bits; decimal input accepts digits only and shares the same ceiling. Bits 0 to 40 are mapped through a fixed table of the 41 capabilities defined in Linux 5.9 and later (cap_chown at 0 through cap_checkpoint_restore at 40, with cap_perfmon and cap_bpf added in 5.8), and set bits above 40 are reported separately as undefined rather than dropped or named. The name list is emitted in ascending number order, comma separated and lowercase, the same form capsh --decode prints; the reverse direction accepts cap_, CAP_ or bare names separated by commas or spaces and rejects an unknown name with the offending token. Outputs are the 16-digit zero-padded hexadecimal mask, the same value without the 0x prefix as /proc/<pid>/status prints, the exact decimal value, a binary rendering in eight-bit groups, the number of set capabilities and the highest one. The page decodes a value the visitor supplies: it executes nothing, stores nothing and makes no network request.
